scope: Entire stored business schema, including all retained project/account data and in-schema version/state records; not just enabled projects or last week's changes.

worker.atomicity: Private dump exit/footer/fsync/streaming hash readback, then atomic current-pointer publish, then exact predecessor cleanup. Transient multiple files allowed. Failures never delete the current verified generation. Metadata is not a live process probe.
worker.recovery: Published but unfinished cleanup is journal-resumed before a fresh weekly backup. Pre-publication crash/unknown artifacts require operator review and block additional generations. No automatic SQL restore.
worker.legacy: At install, freeze exact five 2026-10-13..17 daily SQL/complete pairs by size/SHA. Only after a new weekly backup is published can unchanged approved predecessors be removed. Unknown/changed files are retained.

http.status: GET /api/operations/database-backup; small metadata and file length only; available/latest/lastAttempt/schedule/retention; policy is not proof of enabled timer
http.download: GET /api/operations/database-backup/download?generation=<displayed uuid32>; opened same handle hashed then streamed in 64KiB buffers; native browser download, no whole-file frontend blob
http.writes: No create/delete/run/restore route; protected automatic backup is not a user-uploaded file.

limits: Single-transaction logical dump requires all base tables InnoDB; read-only metadata check before dump.
Same-host backup does not protect against host/disk loss; operator must download to a separate location.
File hash checks are not a database restore rehearsal.
Single retention removes earlier weekly recovery points; data after latest snapshot may need to be recollected/reimported.
Legacy A UI remains compatible with the shared backend but does not gain B's new operations sections/backup card.
